RISK GROUPS  
5 Pedestrians
Pedestrians are particularly vulnerable, because in the event of a collision they are more likely to suffer serious injury.
Statistics indicate that the probability of being killed in a collision is greater on main roads than in built-up areas, mainly due to high speeds. However, most pedestrian deaths from car accidents occur on urban roads, which is where pedestrians are more often hit by vehicles.
This high accident rate is linked mostly to the zone of uncertainty of pedestrians, making their movements less predictable than those of other road users, which means that the driver finds it harder to anticipate their behaviour and actions.
(Página 251 del manual 'Learning to drive')

12 The heat
High temperatures, present a potential risk that may compromise road safety. A temperature of 35 °C inside the vehicle can constitute a danger similar to that of a blood alcohol level of 0,5 g/l.
Heat increases the driver’s reaction time. The driver is likely to make more mistakes, suffer from fatigue, become sleepy and more easily distracted.
Heat increases the risk of the driver becoming aggressive and hostile towards other drivers and road users.
(Página 233 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Safe driving  
 
12 The heat
Driving in day time heat:
Use the air conditioning or the climate control, and ensure that the interior temperature is between 20 and 23 ºC.
Take more rests when travelling long distances, as fatigue will occur quicker.
Drink water or juices often.
Take extra care and caution when driving after eating, as heat promotes the need to sleep.
Wear lightweight and loose clothing.
In summer and when there is sunshine, inside a dark coloured vehicle, the temperature can be ten degrees higher than in a lighter coloured vehicle.

ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES      
       
4 Wheels    
4.2 Tyres  
4.2.3 The tread pattern
The tread pattern is the set of grooves in the tread of a tire. In addition to gripping the road surface, it must guarantee good drainage away of the surface water from the tyre. The adhesion between the tyre and the road is reduced when the tyre is worn.
All tyres, (including retreads) must always comply with the legal requirements. This includes, not only the tyre tread and depth of pattern but also other abnormalities relating to the tyre-wall and tread, inflation pressure, bulges, exposed cords, cuts and other signs of irregular wear, and also the mixing of tyres etc. Basically the carcass (housing) must comply with all legal requirements.
Tyres must, throughout their use on public roads, have a depth in the main grooves of the tread which must be at least:
1.6 millimetres for vehicles in categories M1, N1, O1 and O2.
1.0 millimetres for vehicles in categories M2, M3, N2, N3, O3 and O4.
(Página 70 del manual 'Learning to drive')

ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES

4.2 Tyres

The main grooves are the longitudinal and transverse grooves that form part of the primary tread pattern.
There is no obligation for a motorcycle to have a minimum depth of tyre tread; but the recommendation is that, it should be at least 1.6 millimetres.

Do not travel in parallel (adjacent) to a twowheeled vehicle.
Maintain an adequate and safe separation distance, especially in town, where the two wheeled vehicle will travel easier and may advance quicker than anticipated.

Safe driving  
   
5 Driving in rain
5.1 Adhesion - Grip
In order to maintain the best possible adherence (grip) between your vehicle and the road surface – you should:
Brake smoothly and early, as the wheels can be blocked more easily.
Remember that if you drive through excessive water, there is the possibility that after passing through it, that the brakes (shoes or brake-linings) may be wet and momentarily ineffective. Check your brakes. Step lightly on the brakes so that they make contact with the drums or discs. This will enable the humidity to be eliminated –through the heat (drying effect) produced by friction.
(Página 228 del manual 'Learning to drive')

5 Pedestrians
 
5.3 Walking at night
Outside built-up-areas, between sunset and sunrise or in meteorological or environmental conditions that significantly reduce visibility, all pedestrians, when moving along the road or hard shoulder, must be equipped with a luminous or retro reflective homologated element which is visible at a minimum distance of 150 metres for drivers approaching them.

5 Generic speed        
         
5.1 Maximum speed limits on interurban roads         
5.1.1 Motorways and dual carriageways
Automobiles should never exceed the maximum speed limit applicable to the type of vehicle when driving on motorways and dual carriageways - not even when over taking.
Passenger cars, motorbikes, three-wheeled vehicles similar to motorbikes, camper vans with a Maximum Authorised Mass ≤ 3,500 kg and pick-up trucks: 120 km/h.
Buses, passenger car derivatives and mixed adaptable vehicles: 100 km/h.
Lorries, trailers, vans, camper vans with a Maximum Authorised Mass > 3,500 kg, articulated vehicles, cars with a trailer and all other vehicles: 90 km/h.
Motor tricycles not assimilated to motorcycles and heavy quadricycle: 70 km/h.
 
(Página 172 del manual 'Learning to drive')
